verdict.rationale: Apple's own docs confirm an on-chip Media Engine on M4 Max with two video encode engines and two ProRes encode and decode engines, plus multi-stream 4K ProRes performance for videographers. The ProRes-class part of the story is documented, but the pack never names the codecs the generic video engines handle. Missing for 10: explicit AV1 decode/encode documentation, explicit HEVC/H.264 hardware encode/decode documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration of media engine performance for editing and streaming.

support.subject: As a creator, hardware media engines carry my editing and streaming — documented hardware encode and decode (AV1, HEVC, ProRes-class) on the chip itself

citations.quote: The enhanced Media Engine of M4 Max includes two video encode engines and two ProRes accelerators, making it the ultimate choice for video professionals.
Two ProRes encode and decode engines
with the powerful Media Engine in M4 Max, which features two ProRes accelerators, Mac Studio performance is outstanding for videographers who can effortlessly work with multiple streams of 4K ProRes.
